summary: Oxford County, ME: wood tower 1914, 36-ft steel tower 1919, cab removed 1959, 38-ft platform 1997; FFLA lists it standing with cab gone.

facts.design: 36-foot steel tower built 1919 after a 1914 wood tower; a 38-foot observation platform was built in 1997
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the structure as standing with its cab no longer in place; the cab was removed in 1959. A Summitseeker guide describes a restored tower with a cab, which conflicts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: WillhiteWeb and the Wight obituary both date the cab's removal to 1959, and FFLA lists the tower with its cab no longer in place. The Summitseeker guide describes a restored tower with a cab to climb. We follow the 1959 removal records, which are older and more specific.

sources.title: Old Speck Mountain: Maine's Third-Highest Peak and the Mahoosuc Challenge

notes_for_editor: Build dates (1914, 1919) and the 36-foot height come only from WillhiteWeb; no second source was found. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Facebook post gives a July 1959 date and names a different warden, but Facebook pages could not be read, so it is not cited. Wikipedia has no tower content. The cab question is the open point: the 1959 records and the FFLA asterisk say no cab, while Summitseeker says there is one. A site check or a recent visitor report would settle it. The Maine lookout list also lists the current record as standing with cab gone, so the brief record needed no correction.
